findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses two independent bools (is_validated, is_sent) instead of a typestate enum, making all four combinations legal including is_validated=false + is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: a packet can be marked sent without ever being validated, violating the domain invariant that sent packets must be validated
findings.fix: replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with a single typestate enum (e.g., PacketState { Pending, Validated, Sent }) that makes the invalid transitions unconstructable

findings.problem: status is a raw String instead of a domain newtype or enum. The string "sent" can be any arbitrary value, and mark_sent blindly overwrites it
findings.failure_mode: status can hold any string ("pending", "deleted", ""), defeating type-level invariants and making it impossible to enumerate valid states at compile time
findings.fix: replace status: String with a domain enum (e.g., PacketState) that is only constructable through its defined variants

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain constraints or newtype wrapper
findings.failure_mode: any string including empty, whitespace, or invalid IDs can exist, and there is no compile-time guarantee that id is non-empty or properly formatted
findings.fix: wrap in a newtype (e.g., struct PacketId(String)) with a fallible constructor that rejects invalid values, or use a proper ID crate

findings.problem: All fields on PacketWorkflow are pub mutable, allowing external code to mutate state without any domain enforcement
findings.failure_mode: any caller can do item.is_sent = true directly, completely bypassing mark_sent and its (missing) precondition checks
findings.fix: make all fields private (no pub), provide a fallible constructor, and expose only domain-safe methods or a pure function API

findings.problem: mark_sent returns PacketWorkflow directly with no Result type, so there is no error path when the packet is not validated or otherwise ineligible to be sent
findings.failure_mode: calling mark_sent on an unvalidated packet silently produces an invalid state; callers have no way to detect or handle the precondition failure
findings.fix: return Result<PacketWorkflow, SendError> where SendError encodes why the packet cannot be sent (e.g., NotValidated, AlreadySent)

findings.problem: mark_sent does not check is_validated before allowing the sent transition
findings.failure_mode: a packet in invalid state transitions to sent, permanently recording a sent-but-not-validated packet that violates the domain contract
findings.fix: check is_validated (or the typestate equivalent) and return Err if the precondition is not met

findings.problem: Both status: String and is_sent: bool encode overlapping state. is_sent is derived from status being "sent", yet both are independently mutable
findings.failure_mode: status can be "sent" while is_sent is false (or vice versa), creating inconsistent internal state that any consumer cannot trust
findings.fix: eliminate the redundancy entirely by using a single typestate enum. If a sent timestamp is needed, keep sent_at_epoch_ms as the only sent-time indicator

findings.problem: mark_sent hardcodes status = "sent".to_string() instead of transitioning through a domain type. The to_string() allocates a new String each call
findings.failure_mode: allocates on every call to mark_sent, and the magic string "sent" is not validated against any domain enum. Any future caller that sets status to a different string creates an inconsistent state
findings.fix: transition through a typestate enum variant (e.g., PacketState::Sent) instead of string assignment. The enum variant carries no allocation overhead for the state itself

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for mark_sent or any performance-sensitive path
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify that the allocation-heavy approach (String, to_string, bool flags) meets performance requirements under load
findings.fix: add a micro-benchmark in benches/ measuring mark_sent throughput and allocation count with criterion

findings.problem: No allocation analysis or profiler evidence. mark_sent allocates via .to_string() on every call and uses String (heap) for id and status
findings.failure_mode: in a high-throughput path, repeated String allocations on every mark_sent call could become a bottleneck compared to an enum-based approach with zero allocation
findings.fix: profile with cargo-flamegraph or alloc counter; if hot path, replace String fields with enum typestates to eliminate all allocations in mark_sent

findings.problem: No command evidence (cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test) was run or reported for this crate
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify the crate compiles cleanly, passes clippy, or has any test coverage
findings.fix: run cargo fmt --check && cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features && cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput
no profiler evidence for allocation count in the hot path
no cargo check/clippy/test command evidence reported
no command evidence for release build validation
residual_risk: The crate compiles but structurally cannot enforce its own domain invariants. All fields are publicly mutable, state is split across redundant primitive fields (status String + is_sent bool), and mark_sent has no precondition checks or error type. A single refactor to a typestate enum with private fields, a fallible constructor, and a Result-returning mark_sent would resolve all BLOCKER findings. The current code is a working but incorrect prototype that permits every invalid state it was designed to prevent.
